 Team India supporters rally behind Men in Blue before 2nd T20I 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 24 October 2026, 11:22 am 
 2 min read
 24 Oct 2026 
 ANI Photo | Team India supporters rally behind Men in Blue before 2nd T20I 
 Supporters of Team India gathered in Christchurch ahead of the second T20I against New Zealand at Hagley Oval on October 24, expressing their enthusiasm for the match and the Indian squad.
 India, captained by Shreyas Iyer, secured a thrilling victory in the first T20I by chasing down a target of 226 set by New Zealand, reaching the total with two balls remaining to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.

 Fans queued outside the venue early, showing strong support for the Men in Blue. Suresh Patel said, “I am visiting my children here in New Zealand. I am lucky to be able to watch the India-New Zealand match. I am fully supporting Team India. We are excited for the second T20I, so excited that we have come here three hours prior to queue up ahead of the match.”
 Another supporter, a New Zealander, expressed hopes that India would win not only the T20Is but also the ODIs and both Test matches, adding, “I am from New Zealand, but I consider India my home and support them with all my heart. We are excited for the match.”
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Shruti, another fan, expressed confidence in the Indian team’s chances and said she was eager to see Vaibhav Sooryavanshi play. “Very excited, we’re so excited to watch the match and see the Indian team play here. And last time too, India performed really well; we’ll do it this time as well. We have full faith in the Indian team. We’re very excited to see Vaibhav Sooryavanshi play as well,” she said.
 With Ishan Kishan ruled out of the second T20I due to a low-grade right adductor strain, Sooryavanshi is expected to open for India.
 India enters the second T20I leading the series 1-0 after their four-wicket victory in the opener. Sanju Samson made 67 runs off 33 balls, laying the foundation for the chase, while Naman Dhir hit an unbeaten 42 from 15 deliveries to secure the win with two balls to spare. Captain Shreyas Iyer also contributed 42 runs from 28 balls.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Earlier, New Zealand set a target of 226 for India, their highest total in a home T20I, with Glenn Phillips unbeaten on 82 off 40 balls and Finn Allen scoring 45 from 24 deliveries.
